kef_airport.note: Be at the rental depot by 20:45 — shuttle and damage check eat 45 minutes before a 22:30 bag drop.

gunnuhver.name: Gunnuhver hot springs
gunnuhver.activity: Geothermal steam vents and mud pool

brimketill.name: Brimketill lava pool
brimketill.note: Skip if the weather is poor — it's a viewing platform, nothing more.
brimketill.activity: Lava rock pool on the coast

sky_lagoon.name: Sky Lagoon
sky_lagoon.note: Geothermal lagoon on the Reykjavík shoreline with an infinity edge over the Atlantic. The seven-step ritual is the draw.
sky_lagoon.activity: Geothermal lagoon on the Reykjavík shoreline with an infinity edge over the Atlantic. The seven-step ritual is the draw.

reykjavik.name: Reykjavík
reykjavik.note: Slow morning — checkout, coffee, Hallgrímskirkja or the harbour. Nothing starts before noon.

thingvellir.name: Þingvellir National Park
thingvellir.note: 1,000 ISK parking, covers all lots all day.

bruarfoss.name: Brúarfoss
bruarfoss.note: The bluest water in Iceland, over a stepped falls. A 3.5 km each-way walk from the car park keeps the crowds off.
bruarfoss.activity: The bluest water in Iceland, over a stepped falls. A 3.5 km each-way walk from the car park keeps the crowds off.

geysir.name: Geysir & Strokkur
geysir.note: One of the few reliable sit-down coffee stops on the route.
geysir.activity: Strokkur eruptions + lunch at the café

gullfoss.name: Gullfoss
gullfoss.note: Upper platform is less exposed in wind.

secret_lagoon.name: Secret Lagoon, Flúðir
secret_lagoon.note: Iceland's oldest swimming pool, at Flúðir — a plain hot pool in a field with a small geyser beside it. Far cheaper than the Blue Lagoon.
secret_lagoon.activity: Iceland's oldest swimming pool, at Flúðir — a plain hot pool in a field with a small geyser beside it. Far cheaper than the Blue Lagoon.

kerid.name: Kerið crater
kerid.note: 600 ISK per person. First thing to cut if running late.
kerid.activity: Red crater with a blue lake

reykjadalur.name: Reykjadalur hot river
reykjadalur.note: Free, and the reason Secret Lagoon was cut from Day 1. Bring a towel and shoes you don't mind wetting.
reykjadalur.activity: Hot-river valley — 3 km uphill, then soak in the stream

seljalandsfoss.name: Seljalandsfoss
seljalandsfoss.note: Faces west — the golden-hour slot, and the whole reason this day runs east-to-west. You will get soaked; bring waterproofs.

skogafoss.name: Skógafoss
skogafoss.note: Café here, and the glacier tour eats the middle of the day — make this lunch. Kvernufoss is 10 min away and takes 40 if you are ahead.

kvernufoss.name: Kvernufoss
kvernufoss.note: A waterfall you can walk behind, in a hidden gully ten minutes from Skógafoss and with a fraction of the people.
kvernufoss.activity: A waterfall you can walk behind, in a hidden gully ten minutes from Skógafoss and with a fraction of the people.

solheimajokull.name: Sólheimajökull
solheimajokull.note: Slots are 10:00 or 14:00 only — book 14:00 and be there by 13:40. The 10:00 would cost you the morning's waterfalls.
solheimajokull.activity: Guided glacier hike — a 3 h tour, roughly 1.5 h actually on the ice

dyrholaey.name: Dyrhólaey
dyrholaey.note: Check the access gate is open.

reynisfjara.name: Reynisfjara
reynisfjara.note: Sneaker waves kill people here. Never turn your back on the sea.

vikurfjara.name: Víkurfjara beach
vikurfjara.note: Vík's own black beach, straight off the village — the same black sand and surf as Reynisfjara but without the crowds or the sneaker-wave headland.
vikurfjara.activity: Vík's own black beach, straight off the village — the same black sand and surf as Reynisfjara but without the crowds or the sneaker-wave headland.

klaustur.name: Kirkjubæjarklaustur
klaustur.note: Two nights here — the only real village on this stretch, and Hof/Freysnes has no availability. Rate is my estimate, not a quote.

skaftafell.name: Skaftafell / Svartifoss
skaftafell.note: 45 min uphill each way. Finishes right at dusk — bring a headtorch.

hof.name: Hof í Öræfum
hof.note: Night 4. Book this one FIRST — the Öræfi corridor has the least accommodation in the country.

mulagljufur.name: Múlagljúfur canyon
mulagljufur.note: 3.9 km round trip, 315 m of climb — 1.5-2 h, slower on October mud. Guides call summer-to-September the reliable window. First thing to cut if the morning is wet: it costs only ~20 min of driving but 2.5 h of the day.
mulagljufur.activity: Moss-walled canyon, waterfall at the head

fjallsarlon.name: Fjallsárlón
fjallsarlon.activity: Quieter lagoon, glacier tongue up close

jokulsarlon.name: Jökulsárlón
jokulsarlon.note: Amphibian, 7,100 ISK, 30-40 min. October window is 10:00-17:00 — take the earliest slot the day allows, because a wind cancellation is only rebookable while it is light.
jokulsarlon.activity: Boat tour among the icebergs + lagoon walk

diamond_beach.name: Diamond Beach (Breiðamerkursandur)
diamond_beach.note: Low October light is ideal here.
diamond_beach.activity: Ice boulders on black sand + lunch

stokksnes.name: Stokksnes / Vestrahorn
stokksnes.note: Vestrahorn's jagged peaks rising straight off black dunes — the best single landscape on either route. Private land, small entry fee at the café.
stokksnes.activity: Vestrahorn's jagged peaks rising straight off black dunes — the best single landscape on either route. Private land, small entry fee at the café.

practical.daily_checks: Wind is the real disruptor, not cold. Anything over 15 m/s makes waterfall stops miserable and can tear a car door off its hinges — always hold doors when opening.
practical.fuel_cards: Icelandic self-service pumps need a 4-digit PIN on a foreign chip card. Set this up before you fly. Choose a fixed amount rather than 'fill up' to avoid a large pre-authorisation hold.

closed_in_october.note: Highland F-road, shut by late September
Highland F-road, shut by late September
Usually not open until mid-November. Katla is the alternative

practical.volcanic_status: The Reykjanes peninsula has erupted repeatedly since 2023–24 near Sundhnúkur/Grindavík. Grindavík town remains largely restricted; the Blue Lagoon is open as of mid-2026. Conditions change fast — check almannavarnir.is and vedur.is on the day.
practical.northern_lights: Genuinely possible from Day 2 onward. Check the aurora forecast on vedur.is each evening (combined cloud cover + Kp). Get clear of town lights. Best bases: Hvolsvöllur, Hof, Grundarfjörður.
practical.coffee_reality: Outside Reykjavík and the Golden Circle, cafés are sparse and many rural ones cut hours in October. Reliable sit-down stops: Geysir, Skógafoss, Vík, Arnarstapi, Hraunfossar. Everywhere else it's an N1 petrol station — which is fine, but not a lingering experience.
practical.fuel_stops: Fill up at Vík and at Kirkjubæjarklaustur or Höfn. Do not assume you'll find a station further east.
